claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was a Christian theologian in the Church of Alexandria who taught for about half a century.
Didymus the Blind was born c. 313 and died c. 398.
Didymus became blind at the age of four, before he had learned to read.
Didymus was a student of Origen.
Didymus remained a layman all his life.

Didymus is credited with composing a commentary on almost every book of the Old and New Testaments; however, these commentaries are witnessed to only in fragments of the Biblical chains, or excerpts, found among the papyri at Toura.
In 1941, a large cache of papyri preserving the writings of Origen and Didymus the Blind were discovered in Tura, Egypt.
The Tura find restored otherwise unattested treatises by Didymus the Blind.
Didymus was a leading opponent of Arianism.
Didymus staunchly defended the doctrine of the Trinity.

Didymus was thoroughly orthodox in the doctrine of the Trinity, but at the same time a great venerator of Origen, and a participant of his peculiar views concerning the pre-existence of souls, and probably concerning final restoration.
